subtopics.title: Oscars 2026 and Indian Oscar winners
subtopics.summary: The 98th Academy Awards were held in Los Angeles to celebrate excellence in global cinema, and the Oscars are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (USA). The 2026 Best Picture was One Battle After Another, and Paul Thomas Anderson won Best Director. The booklet also records Oscar milestones, such as Wings as the first Best Picture winner and Walt Disney's record of 22 Oscars.
facts: The 98th Academy Awards were held in Los Angeles to celebrate excellence in global cinema.
The Oscars are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (USA).
Louis B. Mayer, co-founder of MGM Studios, conceptualised the Oscars.
The Oscars honour artistic and technical achievements, including acting, directing and writing.
Oscar categories started at 12 and have now expanded to 24.
The Oscar statuette is gold-plated bronze and shows a knight standing on a reel of film holding a sword.
Wings was the first Best Picture winner.
Walt Disney holds the record for the most Oscars (22).
Katharine Hepburn leads in acting wins, with 4 Best Actress awards.
2026: Best Picture was One Battle After Another; Best Director was Paul Thomas Anderson.
Indian winners at the Academy Awards listed in the booklet include Bhanu Athaiya, Guneet Monga and Resul Pookutty.

subtopics.title: BAFTA Awards 2026 and India's BAFTA history
subtopics.summary: The British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA) presents its awards annually from London. At the 2026 BAFTA Awards, One Battle After Another won Best Film and Hamnet won Outstanding British Film. Boong, a Manipuri film, became the first Indian film to win Best Children's and Family Film, and earlier Indian milestones include Rohini Hattangadi's win and A.R. Rahman's Best Film Music award.
facts: BAFTA was established in 1947 and presents its awards annually.
BAFTA is presented by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts and is based in London, United Kingdom.
BAFTA covers Film, Television, Games and Children's & Family Content.
2026 Best Film: One Battle After Another; Best Director: Paul Thomas Anderson.
2026 Outstanding British Film: Hamnet; Best Leading Actress: Jessie Buckley (Hamnet).
2026 Best Leading Actor: Robert Aramayo (I Swear).
Boong became the first Indian film to win Best Children's and Family Film at the BAFTA Awards 2026.
Boong is a Manipuri film directed by Lakshmipriya Devi and produced by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani.
Rohini Hattangadi was the first Indian actor to win a competitive BAFTA, for Best Supporting Actress in Gandhi (1983).
Asif Kapadia won Best British Film for The Warrior (2002); A.R. Rahman won Best Film Music for Slumdog Millionaire (2009).

subtopics.title: Jnanpith and Sahitya Akademi awards
subtopics.summary: R. Vairamuthu was selected for the 60th Jnanpith Award 2025, becoming the third Tamil writer to receive it. The Jnanpith, instituted in 1961, is India's oldest and highest literary honour and is not awarded posthumously. The Sahitya Akademi Awards 2025 honoured 24 authors for outstanding literary works across Indian languages.
facts: R. Vairamuthu was selected for the 60th Jnanpith Award 2025.
Vairamuthu is the third Tamil writer to receive the Jnanpith, after Akilan (1975) and Jayakanthan (2002).
Vairamuthu is the first Tamil writer primarily recognised for poetry to receive the Jnanpith.
The Jnanpith was instituted in 1961 and established by Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain and his wife Rama Jain.
The first Jnanpith was awarded in 1965 to G. Sankara Kurup, a Malayalam writer.
Ashapoorna Devi (1976, Prothom Protishruti) was the first woman recipient of the Jnanpith.
Amitav Ghosh (2018) was the first English-language winner of the Jnanpith.
The Jnanpith recognises lifetime contribution, is not awarded posthumously and is given to Indian authors only.
Sahitya Akademi Awards 2025 honoured 24 authors, including Navtej Sarna for Crimson Spring (English novel).
Sahitya Akademi Awards are awarded to Indian citizens and cover 24 languages, including English and Rajasthani.

subtopics.title: ASMITA Initiative
subtopics.summary: ASMITA stands for Achieving Sports Milestone by Inspiring Women Through Action and was launched in 2021 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. It was earlier known as Khelo India Women's League. The initiative aims to promote sports participation among girls and women at the grassroots level and to identify and nurture young sporting talent, especially from rural and tribal areas.

quizzes.passage: The Academy Awards, popularly known as the Oscars, are among the best-known honours in the film industry. The 98th edition of the awards was held in Los Angeles to celebrate excellence in global cinema. The awards recognise artistic and technical achievements, and they cover a wide range of work, including acting, directing and writing. They are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, an organisation based in the United States. The annual ceremony takes place at the Dolby Theatre in Los Angeles. Over the years the awards have grown in scope, and new categories have been added to reflect different kinds of cinematic work. Each year the winners in the main categories are widely discussed, and their names become part of the record of world cinema. Students of current affairs are expected to know the year of the ceremony, the city where it is held and the body that presents the awards, since these basic details are often used in questions. The awards also show how the film industry has changed, because the categories and winners reflect the priorities of each period. Because the awards cover technical as well as artistic work, they recognise many of the people who contribute to a film. Keeping these basic details in mind helps a candidate answer questions on the Oscars with confidence.

quizzes.passage: India honours its writers through several prestigious literary awards. Among these, the Jnanpith Award is regarded as one of the country's oldest and highest literary honours, and it is often compared to a Nobel Prize for Indian literature. The award is given only to Indian authors for outstanding contributions to literature, and it recognises lifetime work rather than a single book. It is not awarded posthumously. The works considered can be in any of the languages listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, as well as English. The award is presented by Bharatiya Jnanpith. Another major honour is the Sahitya Akademi Award, which recognises outstanding literary works and is given to Indian citizens across many languages. Each year the Sahitya Akademi announces its awards, recognising authors for literary excellence in different languages and genres, from novels to memoirs. Together, these awards highlight the range of literature produced in India and give writers national recognition for their contribution to Indian letters. The Jnanpith is awarded for a writer's overall body of work rather than one book or one year of writing, so each recognition reflects sustained literary effort. Awards of this kind also help readers discover writing in many languages, from the languages of the Eighth Schedule to English, and they show how literature in India is shared across regions and communities.
